findings.highlight: what should we do if we win the Holy Grail War
findings.evidenceJa: 聖杯を手に入れたらどうするか
findings.governingReading: What should they do once they obtain the Grail?
findings.explanation: The English repeats winning the war and removes the question about what to do with the prize afterward.

findings.highlight: I don’t care who uses the Holy Grail.
findings.evidenceJa: 聖杯の使い道なんてどうでもいいわ
findings.governingReading: Illya does not care what use is made of the Grail.
findings.explanation: The English changes indifference to the Grail’s use into indifference about the identity of its user.

findings.highlight: Saber’s acting in a complicated manner
findings.evidenceJa: その様子がただ事ではない
findings.governingReading: Her state is clearly no ordinary matter.
findings.explanation: The awkward English weakens the visible gravity that makes Rin and Illya stop arguing.

findings.highlight: I do not know how powerful the Holy Grail is.
findings.evidenceJa: 聖杯がどれほどの許容範囲を持っているかは知らない
findings.governingReading: She does not know the range or scope of what the Grail can accommodate.
findings.explanation: The English replaces uncertainty about the Grail’s applicable scope with a generic power-level question.

findings.highlight: you’re respected as a heroic spirit
findings.evidenceJa: 英霊として奉られている
findings.governingReading: one is enshrined or worshipped as a Heroic Spirit
findings.explanation: Respected weakens the supernatural posthumous status Rin uses to explain why a Heroic Spirit cannot ordinarily intervene by choice.

findings.highlight: they’re summoned as heroic spirits
findings.evidenceJa: 英霊として使役される
findings.governingReading: they are made to serve as Heroic Spirits, read as “familiars”
findings.explanation: The English removes both compulsory service and the familiar reading that motivates Shirou’s summary.

findings.highlight: she became a heroic spirit after she died
findings.evidenceJa: 死後も英霊として守護者なんてモノを続けている
findings.governingReading: after death she continues serving as a guardian in the form of a Heroic Spirit
findings.explanation: The English omits the ongoing guardian service that Shirou imagines as the cost of Saber’s supposed bargain.

findings.highlight: I would wield my sword as a heroic spirit after my death
findings.evidenceJa: あらゆるモノの為に剣を執ろう
findings.governingReading: she would take up her sword for all things as a Heroic Spirit after death
findings.explanation: The English removes the universal beneficiary of the service Saber offers in exchange for the Grail.

findings.highlight: return to that stopped point once I obtain the Holy Grail
findings.evidenceJa: 聖杯を求めた後、止まっている場所に戻っている
findings.governingReading: After seeking the Grail in another time, she returns to the point where she is suspended.
findings.explanation: The English says she returns after obtaining the Grail, contradicting the explanation that only successful acquisition ends the cycle and lets her die.

findings.highlight: summoned into various ages
findings.evidenceJa: あらゆる時間上に呼び出され
findings.governingReading: summoned in answer to calls across all points in time
findings.explanation: Various ages weakens the unrestricted temporal scope of Shirou’s tentative model.

findings.highlight: no matter how many times they are summoned into the same age
findings.evidenceJa: あらゆる時代に同時に呼び出されようと
findings.governingReading: even if summoned simultaneously into every era
findings.explanation: The English changes simultaneous manifestations across all eras into repeated summons within one era.

findings.highlight: Saber talks without much interest.
findings.evidenceJa: 淡々とセイバーは語る
findings.governingReading: Saber speaks matter-of-factly and without outward agitation.
findings.explanation: The English assigns lack of interest to Saber during the disclosure of her defining wish.

findings.highlight: my mind is spacing out
findings.evidenceJa: 愕然と意識が白くなって
findings.governingReading: His consciousness goes white with shock.
findings.explanation: Spacing out trivializes the acute bodily shock with casual language.

findings.highlight: she will continue to be summoned to fight
findings.evidenceJa: ただ戦うだけの現象となって使役され続ける
findings.governingReading: She will become a phenomenon that does nothing but fight and remain in service.
findings.explanation: The English removes Saber’s reduction from a person to a battle-only phenomenon and weakens continuous servitude to recurring summons.

findings.highlight: So why don’t you understand
findings.evidenceJa: なんだってそんな事に、おまえだけが気づいていない
findings.governingReading: Why are you the only one who cannot see that?
findings.explanation: The English omits Shirou’s crucial claim that everyone except Saber can recognize what she has already given.

findings.highlight: I’ll be able to try with all my powers
findings.evidenceJa: 俺は全力でこの戦いに
findings.governingReading: He will commit himself fully to this battle.
findings.explanation: The English omits the battle as the object and changes a declaration of commitment into the ability to try.

findings.highlight: can be heard in the distance
findings.evidenceJa: さざ波のように響いてくる
findings.governingReading: The light scraping spreads and resounds like ripples.
findings.explanation: The English invents distance and removes the ripple-like multiplication that foreshadows encirclement.

findings.highlight: A strange sound.
findings.evidenceJa: ガシャガシャという音
findings.governingReading: a repeated hard metallic clatter
findings.explanation: The English replaces a concrete sound effect with an unspecified judgment.

findings.highlight: bugs crawling around a light trap
findings.evidenceJa: 誘蛾灯に群がる虫
findings.governingReading: insects swarming a moth-attracting lamp
findings.explanation: The English changes airborne swarming toward a light into crawling around a trap, weakening the approaching mob image.

findings.highlight: I can sense that many sources of magical energy surround this place.
findings.evidenceJa: 複数の人間によるモノだってのは感じ取れる
findings.governingReading: He can sense that the encircling magical energy comes from multiple humans.
findings.explanation: The English removes the apparently human origin whose conflict with their hollow lack of will drives the identification puzzle.
